transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?
What scared me enough to come in is that after I eat too much, I’ve been making myself throw up so I won’t gain weight. It’s not just a one-time mistake anymore.
When this happens, do you eat an unusually large amount of food before you make yourself throw up?

Yes. After a bridge night or a late shift, I can come home and eat leftover casserole, cookies I baked, crackers, ice cream—just all of it in one sitting. It’s much more than I’d ever put on a plate if anyone else were around.
During those eating episodes, do you feel unable to stop or control how much you’re eating?
Yes. Once I start, it’s like I’m on automatic. I keep thinking I should stop, especially before my husband notices, but I still reach for one more thing.
How much does your body weight or shape affect how you feel about yourself?

A lot, honestly. If my skirt feels tight before church, or I catch myself from the side in one of the store mirrors, it can ruin my whole day. I just feel like everybody can see that I’ve let myself go.
How often do these binge-and-vomit episodes happen?
For the past several months, it’s been most weeks. I’ll have one of those secret eating spells and then make myself sick afterward. I can’t really say it’s just occasional anymore.
Are you currently at a significantly low body weight for your height?
I’m not sure what counts as significantly low. I don’t think of myself as underweight, no.
